title: Resource Requests, Limits & Autoscaling
intro: Pods that don't declare resource requests/limits can starve their neighbors or get OOMKilled unpredictably. Let's look at how usage, limits, and autoscaling fit together.

steps.prompt: Check current CPU/memory usage across all pods.
steps.explanation: This is live usage, not the requests/limits configured in the spec — comparing the two is how you catch a pod that's about to hit its memory limit.
steps.why: 'kubectl describe pod' shows configured limits but not live usage — 'top' is the only place you see what's actually being consumed right now.

steps.prompt: Check if this namespace has a ResourceQuota capping total usage.
steps.fake_output:
NAME      REQUESTS.CPU   REQUESTS.MEMORY   LIMITS.CPU   LIMITS.MEMORY
compute   2/4            4Gi/8Gi           4/8          8Gi/16Gi
steps.explanation: A ResourceQuota caps the TOTAL requests/limits across every pod in the namespace — this is why a new pod can fail to schedule even when individual nodes have room.
steps.why: This is a namespace-wide cap, different from a single pod's own limits — a pod can be well within its own resource limit and still get rejected if the namespace as a whole is already at quota.

steps.prompt: Check if there's a HorizontalPodAutoscaler configured for the 'web' deployment.
steps.fake_output:
NAME   REFERENCE          TARGETS         MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS   AGE
web    Deployment/web     45%/80% cpu     2         10        3          1h
steps.explanation: An HPA watches a metric (here, CPU) and adjusts the Deployment's replica count automatically between MINPODS and MAXPODS.
steps.why: This replaces manually running 'kubectl scale' during traffic spikes — once an HPA exists, don't fight it by scaling manually, since it'll just override your manual change on its next check.

steps.prompt: Create an HPA for the 'web' deployment: scale between 2 and 10 pods, targeting 80% CPU.
steps.explanation: This is the quick way to create an HPA — equivalent to writing and applying a full HPA manifest.
steps.why: For anything beyond simple CPU-percent scaling (custom metrics, scaling on requests-per-second) you'd need a full HPA YAML instead — 'autoscale' only covers this common CPU-based case.
